- When sentiment is positive (≥0.4) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast slightly to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and forecast is below recent low, increase forecast gently to avoid underreaction.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak at 1.5x recent 7-day average.  
- If true outcome consistently lags forecast by 1–3 days, adjust forward-looking forecasts to align with 3-day lagged mean.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.2) and forecast is volatile, apply smoothing filter to reduce noise and avoid false extremes.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast mean is >10% above true mean, reduce by 5–10% to account for mean reversion bias.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.0 values, assume low confidence — reduce forecast volatility by 20–30%.
